about: Rover settings definition, owned by Trail_Tracer_Mower (docs/settings_def.json). The PC uses an unchanged copy. Words from the PC draft (Trail-Tracer-PC-Telemetry 22deeea); values checked against src/usb_msc_fat.cpp (defaults, limits) and src/main.cpp (STATIONARY_KEYS). Format: Trail-Tracer-PC-Telemetry docs/control_api.md, section 3. 'list' ends 'end <n> def 6'. Version 6: groups in user order ('groups'), a 'label' per setting, DSP settings (dsp_*) with read-only values in effect (dsp_*_eff, 'readonly': true; 'effect' names the _eff key of a setting). Version 7 (firmware 0.5.69): 'string' and 'choice' types, 'max_len', 'pattern' and 'dec'; the servo outputs by function (steer_*, throttle_*) replace PWM_OUT_n_*; drive_output, vehicle_name, steer_lpf_hz; CHARGE_MAX_SECONDS is the charge time. Version 8 (firmware 0.5.71): radio_mode (espnow or wifi, from the next start), read-only wifi_ssid and wifi_password (set or not set; USB 'wifi set' writes them). Version 9 (firmware 0.5.87): dsp_sweep_bins (off, auto or 1-8; the bins off that sweep 41.1-68.5 kHz; default auto).

rover_mode.description: What drive mode 2 (autonomous) runs. rover: the full mission (roam, bounce, return, join, follow, dock, depart). follow only: find the wire, join it, follow it. In both the rover drives straight off the wire and steers on position only after the join. position follower (expert): the plain position-steering wire follower, which circles when it starts off the wire. Cruise mode (RC throttle) always uses the wire follower

rover_goal_cw.description: Direction along the wire into the charger: true = clockwise seen from above
rover_goal_cw.label: Charger direction clockwise

rover_sensor_height_mm.description: Distance of the sensor centre above the wire
rover_sensor_height_mm.label: Sensor height

rover_seek_vbatt.description: Return to the wire below this battery voltage (filtered; 0 = off, else 6 to 26)
rover_seek_vbatt.label: Return below this voltage

rover_entry_btx.description: Beacon channel before the charger: slow approach (0 = none)
rover_entry_btx.label: Beacon before the charger

rover_exit_btx.description: Beacon channel after the charger exit: the vehicle turns back if it meets this beacon first (0 = none)
rover_exit_btx.label: Beacon after the charger

rover_lost_timeout_s.description: The autopilot halts after this long without the wire (0 = never)
rover_lost_timeout_s.label: Stop after wire lost for

espnow_enabled.description: Telemetry messages over ESP-NOW. If telemetry_enabled is also false, the vehicle takes no commands. The vehicle refuses false over ESP-NOW
espnow_enabled.label: Radio messages

telemetry_rate_hz.description: Vehicle log sample rate in Hz. Below 100 Hz an anti-alias filter (two moving averages) runs first. Other values go to the nearest allowed rate
telemetry_rate_hz.label: Log rate

telemetry_bins_hz.description: Rate in Hz of the coil magnitudes of all 8 frequency bins in the vehicle log, for the per-bin plots. The same anti-alias filter as the log rate runs first. 0 = off
telemetry_bins_hz.label: Coil plot rate

espnow_tx_power_dbm.description: Radio transmit power in dBm, 0.25 dB steps. 19.5 is the radio's maximum. A low power over the radio can lose the link to this vehicle
espnow_tx_power_dbm.label: Radio power

telemetry_enabled.description: Vehicle log over ESP-NOW. If espnow_enabled is also false, the vehicle takes no commands. The vehicle refuses false over ESP-NOW
telemetry_enabled.label: Telemetry

radio_mode.label: Radio link
radio_mode.description: How the vehicle sends its telemetry. espnow: straight to a monitor, with no network. wifi: through a Wi-Fi network to the PC telemetry server; the vehicle then takes no commands over the radio. A change takes effect after a save and a restart. The vehicle refuses wifi over ESP-NOW.

wifi_ssid.label: Wi-Fi network
wifi_ssid.description: The network name for radio_mode wifi. Set it over USB with: wifi set <network> <password>. The vehicle keeps it in its own memory, not in config.json.

wifi_password.label: Wi-Fi password
wifi_password.description: Shows set or not set. The vehicle never shows or sends the password. Set it over USB with the wifi set command.

cmd_key.description: Fleet password; 0 = blank (accepts key 0); USB or config.json only
cmd_key.label: Fleet password

dsp_frame_period_us.label: Update period
dsp_frame_period_us.description: Time between two position updates from the sensor board. A longer period averages more signal: less noise, slower response. The board uses the nearest period that it can make. Default 10000 us (10 ms). The sensor board runs set steps: 2354, 2938, 3522 ... us (+584 us a step) with the slow ADC on, 2336, 2628 ... us (+292 us) with it off; a setting runs at the step at or below it. The shortest setting is 2938 us with every link, so the sensor board keeps spare time; the board refuses a shorter one. Below 5000 us the CPU load can pass the 70 % target with Wi-Fi.

dsp_frame_period_us_eff.label: Update period (in effect)
dsp_frame_period_us_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

dsp_sensors.label: Sensors on the board
dsp_sensors.description: Number of wire sensors that the sensor board reads: 1 or 2. With 1 sensor, the board reads it faster.

dsp_sensors_eff.label: Sensors on the board (in effect)
dsp_sensors_eff.description: The value that the sensor board uses now (its answer). Empty until the board answers; it can differ from the setting when the board rounds or limits it.

rover_no_tx_s.label: Stop after no Tx signal for

rover_roam_time_s.description: Rover mode: roam this long, then find the wire, join it and follow it for the follow time; then turn inward and roam again. The time counts only in roam (not while it waits for the Tx signal). A charge return comes first; after a charge both times start again. 0 = off (also when the follow time is 0)
rover_roam_time_s.label: Roam time

rover_follow_time_s.description: Rover mode: after the roam time, follow the wire this long, then stop, turn inward by a random angle (inward turn minimum to maximum) and roam again. A charge return comes first. 0 = off (also when the roam time is 0)
rover_follow_time_s.label: Follow time

rover_follow_exit_deg.description: At the end of a timed follow: the angle between the wire and the new heading, before the bounce spread. 90 = straight into the loop. The bounce spread and the bounce minimum leave angle apply as at a bounce
rover_follow_exit_deg.label: Follow end leave angle

rover_rearm_fall_mm.description: After any turn, the bounce arms again when the wire radius falls this much below its highest value since the turn: the rover closes on the wire again. 30 mm is 3 x the radius noise. More delays the bounce; less lets noise arm it
rover_rearm_fall_mm.label: Re-arm radius fall
